claim: Total on-chain stablecoin settlement reached $33 trillion in 2025, surpassing combined Visa ($16.7T) and Mastercard ($10.6T) volume, but this includes significant non-payment (trading/treasury) activity.
quoted_support: Total on-chain stablecoin settlement reached $33 trillion for the year, surpassing the combined volume of Visa ($16.7 trillion) and Mastercard ($10.6 trillion). That number includes significant trading and treasury activity, not just point-of-sale transactions.

claim: Card processing fees total 1.70-2.05% (card-present) to 2.25-3.50% (e-commerce) of transaction value, versus 0.1-0.3% for stablecoin settlement including on/off-ramp costs — a 10-25x reduction.
stance_target: merchant cost incentive to adopt stablecoin rails
scope_conditions: early 2026 fee schedules, Spark.money (vendor with commercial interest)
quoted_support: total costs for stablecoin settlement typically fall between 0.1% and 0.3% of transaction value. That is a 10x to 25x reduction in payment processing costs.

claim: The GENIUS Act, providing the first US federal stablecoin regulatory framework, was signed into law July 18, 2025, with implementing OCC/FDIC rules due by July 18, 2026.
stance_target: regulatory catalyst timetable for stablecoin adoption
scope_conditions: US federal law, passed Senate 68-30, House 308-122
quoted_support: Passed by the Senate 68-30 and the House 308-122, it was signed into law on July 18, 2025...Implementing regulations must be finalized by July 18, 2026.

claim: The biggest practical barrier to merchant stablecoin adoption is not technology or regulation, but that most consumers still pay with cards.
stance_target: near-term consumer-checkout disruption of Apple Pay/card rails
quoted_support: The biggest practical barrier is not technology or regulation: it is that most consumers still pay with cards.

claim: Stablecoin-linked Visa cards let consumers spend stablecoins at any of Visa's 175 million merchant acceptance points with the merchant receiving ordinary fiat settlement — bridging rather than bypassing card infrastructure.
scope_conditions: Visa/Stripe Bridge partnership, expanding to 100+ countries by end of 2026
quoted_support: These cards let consumers spend stablecoins at any of Visa's 175 million merchant acceptance points, with the merchant receiving fiat settlement through their existing acquirer.
